Our goal is simple: to provide safe, effective, and eco-friendly mold remediation services, backed by scientific expertise and exceptional customer care. Our Story At Mold Master Remediation, we’re passionate about safeguarding homes and families from the dangers of mold and moisture intrusion. Our journey began in 2013 when Kevin started conducting Mold and Stucco Inspections with a specialized focus on moisture management. It quickly became clear that mold was a widespread issue, with approximately 8 out of 10 homes revealing its presence during inspections. ​ Clients often asked us the critical follow-up question once mold was discovered: “What should we do now?” Unfortunately, at the time, we lacked a trusted resource for comprehensive mold remediation. Recognizing this gap in the service market, we set out to create a solution—and Mold Master Remediation was born. Kevin immersed himself in mastering remediation protocols, studying best practices, and refining techniques. After becoming a certified mold remediation contractor, he began delivering solutions that prioritize both safety and effectiveness. ​ What sets Mold Master Remediation apart is our unwavering commitment to two core principles: Non-Toxic Solutions: We exclusively use non-toxic biocides and antimicrobial treatments. Why replace mold toxins with harmful chemicals? Our approach ensures your home is both mold-free and safe for your family and pets. Unmatched Attention to Detail: We treat every step of the remediation process with care and precision. Cutting corners isn’t in our DNA. Unlike others in the industry, we take pride in delivering thorough, long-lasting results you can trust. ​ At Mold Master Remediation, we’re more than a service provider—we’re a partner in restoring healthy environments and peace of mind. Questions? Contact Us VISUAL INSPECTION ​ Mold growth isn’t always easy to detect. It often hides in less obvious areas, like behind walls, under flooring, or inside HVAC systems, making it easy to miss without a trained eye. That’s why combining mold sampling and testing with a detailed visual inspection by an experienced mold inspector is crucial. ​ A skilled inspector conducts a thorough assessment to locate hidden mold growth that might otherwise go unnoticed. These areas of concealed mold can significantly impact your building’s structural integrity and negatively affect indoor air quality, potentially leading to health concerns for occupants. ​ By identifying the source and extent of the problem, a comprehensive visual inspection ensures that remediation efforts target the right areas, effectively addressing the issue and preventing further growth. It’s an essential step in protecting your property and ensuring a safe, healthy environment. INFRARED IMAGING ​ ​ Infrared imaging (thermal imaging) is a non-invasive technology that detects temperature variations on surfaces to uncover hidden issues like moisture intrusion. ​ Key Benefits: Detects Moisture & Temperature Differences: Moisture in building materials shows cooler thermal patterns because it retains heat differently than dry materials. Non-Destructive: Assesses problem areas without drilling or damaging walls. Fast & Accurate: Instantly identifies issues, even in hard-to-reach or large areas. Prevents Bigger Problems: Early detection helps prevent mold growth, structural damage, and costly repairs. Common Uses: Identifying leaks in roofs, walls, or ceilings. Finding condensation from poor ventilation or insulation. Pinpointing plumbing leaks behind walls or under floors. Assessing water damage after floods or heavy rains. While infrared imaging is highly effective, expert interpretation ensures accurate results and guides further action, like repairs or additional testing. ​ ​ ​ MOISTURE ANALYSIS ​ When moisture is detected, specialized tools provide precise measurements: Moisture Meter: Pin-type devices measure retained moisture in building materials. Hygrometer: Monitors relative humidity (RH) to prevent mold, which thrives when RH exceeds 60%. Together, these tools and methods provide a clear picture of moisture levels, ensuring targeted solutions and mold prevention. We use advanced sampling methods to ensure accurate results and a comprehensive understanding of your space. Mold testing is typically performed alongside our Mold Inspections . Please see below for pricing. Schedule Today! AIR SAMPLING - $149/first sample, then $89/additional sample Collects air samples to measure mold spore levels, analyzed in a lab to identify mold types and concentrations. ​ Applications: Detects airborne mold when growth isn’t visible. Assesses indoor air quality by comparing it to outdoor air (requires at least one exterior sample). Strengths: Identifies mold types and spore levels. Detects hidden mold. Evaluates potential air quality risks. Limitations: Results may vary with environmental factors (e.g., weather, time of day). Reflects conditions only at the time of sampling. ​ ​ SURFACE SAMPLING - $149/ first sample, then $89 /additional sample Collects samples from surfaces with visible or suspected mold using swabs, tape, or bulk samples. ​ Applications: Confirms mold presence on surfaces. Identifies specific mold types in affected areas. Strengths: Directly detects mold on surfaces. Targets specific areas of concern. Helps assess the extent of contamination. Limitations: Does not evaluate airborne mold spores or air quality. Limited to the sampled areas. BULK SAMPLING - $149/ first sample, then $89 /additional sample Involves collecting a portion of building material (e.g., drywall, insulation) suspected of harboring mold for lab analysis. Applications: Confirms mold presence within materials. Identifies mold species. Assesses contamination in structural materials. Strengths: Provides detailed mold analysis within materials. Helps determine the depth and severity of infestation. Limitations: Destructive method, requiring material removal. Does not assess airborne mold levels. ​ ​ ERMI (Environmental Relative Moldiness Index) - starting at $395/test A more advanced method that uses DNA-based analysis (qPCR) to identify and quantify mold species in a dust sample. ​ Applications: Offers a comprehensive assessment of mold presence over time. Ideal for long-term indoor environment monitoring. Strengths: Highly accurate and detailed mold species identification. Analyzes cumulative mold exposure from settled dust. Limitations: Higher cost than other methods. Results can be complex and require expert interpretation. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Schedule Today! ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ CHOOSING THE RIGHT METHOD ​ Selecting the right mold testing method depends on your specific situation and goals. Your mold inspector will guide you, but here are some general recommendations: Air Sampling: Best for evaluating indoor air quality and detecting hidden mold spores in the air. Surface or Bulk Sampling: Ideal for confirming visible mold growth or checking contamination within materials like drywall or insulation. ERMI Testing: Recommended for a detailed, long-term assessment of mold presence, particularly for ongoing monitoring. A comprehensive mold inspection often uses a combination of these methods to provide the most accurate and actionable results. Your inspector will work closely with you to assess your needs and determine the best approach for your home or building. ​ ​ ​ UNDERSTANDING YOUR RESULTS AND NEXT STEPS ​ Once the testing is complete, your inspector will guide you through the findings and, if necessary, recommend a customized remediation plan to effectively address any issues and restore a healthy environment in your space. © 2025 by Mold Master Remediation.
